page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance within the Dlsv7 series, provisioned using Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, this instance provides 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 96 GB of system RAM, yielding a lean 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The underlying processor includes a generous 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced hardware extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions for INT8 and BF16 formats), and cryptographic instruction sets such as VAES and SHA-NI.

The compute profile demonstrates high throughput in specialized computational workloads. PassMark testing records strong top-quartile results across aggregate CPU calculations, vector extensions, and encryption suites. Synthetic compression benchmarks highlight exceptional single-threaded and multi-threaded decompression rates, exceeding 303 GB/s on bzip3 workloads. Furthermore, the presence of AMX accelerators aids compact CPU-driven machine learning inference, delivering strong token throughput on small and medium language models. General CPU stress tests reflect moderate compute scalability, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations falling in the middle 50% percentile across comparable instances.

Hardware tradeoffs are centered on storage and memory density. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage, requiring workloads to attach remote Premium Storage volumes for operational persistence. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation prioritizes raw processing density over RAM-heavy footprints, making it cost-efficient for compute-bound operations that do not justify paying for unutilized memory capacity. The system lacks discrete GPU hardware and bundled public IPv4 networking.

Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is well suited for CPU-intensive parallel processing, static web serving infrastructure, encryption tasks, build automation, data compression pipelines, and in-memory key-value layers like Redis that operate within a 96 GB operating envelope.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring a 48-vCPU configuration powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running up to 4.2 GHz across 24 physical cores. Structured with a low-memory 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, the instance supplies 96 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, boosting cryptographic workloads, compression routines, and INT8/BF16 AI inference tasks. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across PassMark computational tests, multi-threaded decompression, and Redis key-value operations, while standard multi-core stress metrics align within median boundaries. The server lacks bundled local disk storage and GPU accelerators, relying on external network-attached block volumes. This hardware distribution serves high-density web servers, CI/CD runners, and computational batch workloads requiring concentrated CPU throughput without redundant memory overhead.
